title: Credit Note and Distributor Ledger Reconciliation
summary: Check that every approved claim became the right credit note, that nothing was credited twice, and that your books and each distributor's ledger agree, with the differences explained.

seo.title: Credit Note and Distributor Ledger Reconciliation
seo.description: Match approved claims to credit notes, catch credits issued twice or never issued, and reconcile your books with each distributor's ledger statement.

problem.intro: Once claims are approved, finance raises credit notes, distributors adjust them against invoices, and at the end of a quarter or year both sides confirm balances. Credit notes are raised in the ERP or Tally from spreadsheets, and distributors keep their own books, so the two drift apart and nobody sees why until the balance confirmation does not match.

pain_points.title: Credits issued twice or never
pain_points.detail: An approved claim is credited twice after a resubmission, or never credited at all, and the gap only shows up months later.

pain_points.title: Amounts that differ from the approval
pain_points.detail: The credit note amount or invoice reference differs from what finance approved, because it was keyed by hand from a sheet.

pain_points.title: Balance confirmations that do not agree
pain_points.detail: Distributor ledger statements and your books disagree, and finding the difference means going through months of entries line by line.

pain_points.title: Disputes without evidence
pain_points.detail: When a distributor says a claim is still pending, the approval, the credit note and the adjustment sit in different files and inboxes.

solution.overview: VipraTech links each approved claim line to the credit note raised for it, and each credit note to the invoice and ledger entry it was adjusted against. It reads distributor ledger statements in whatever format they arrive, compares them with your books entry by entry, and explains each difference: a credit not yet issued, a credit issued twice, a timing difference or an entry missing on one side. Finance reviews the differences, and the system produces a reconciliation statement that can be shared with the distributor.
capabilities: Links every approved claim line to its credit note, and flags approvals with no credit note
Catches credit notes issued twice, for the wrong amount or against the wrong invoice
Reads distributor ledger statements in Excel, PDF or scanned form
Compares each distributor's ledger with your books and explains every difference
Reconciliation statement for each distributor, ready to share
Audit trail from claim approval to credit note to ledger entry

workflow.title: Collect records
workflow.detail: Approved claim sheets, credit notes from the ERP or Tally, and distributor ledger statements are gathered for the period.

workflow.title: Link claims to credit notes
workflow.detail: Each approved claim line is matched to its credit note by distributor, scheme, invoice and amount.

workflow.title: Flag mismatches
workflow.detail: Missing, duplicate and mismatched credit notes are flagged with the approval and the note side by side.

workflow.title: Compare ledgers
workflow.detail: Each distributor's ledger statement is compared with your books, and every difference is given a reason.

workflow.title: Finance review
workflow.detail: Finance confirms corrections and decides what to raise or reverse.

workflow.title: Share the statement
workflow.detail: A reconciliation statement goes to each distributor, and open items are tracked to closure.

match_rules.rule: Every approved claim has a credit note
match_rules.logic: Each approved claim must have one credit note for the approved amount, raised within the agreed time.
Credit note amount, distributor and reference must match the approval. Any difference is flagged.
A credit note with no approved claim behind it is held for review.
Your ledger and the distributor's statement must agree once in-transit items and posting-date differences are listed.
Tax credit notes must carry the original invoice reference where GST rules need it.

exception_codes.meaning: An approved claim has no credit note.
The credit note differs from the approved amount.
exception_codes.action: Correct the credit note or the approval.

exception_codes.meaning: A credit note has no approved claim behind it.
exception_codes.action: Find the approval, or reverse the note.

exception_codes.meaning: An entry appears in one ledger only.
exception_codes.action: Mark as timing, or post the missing entry.

exception_codes.meaning: A tax credit note does not reference the original invoice.

inputs: Approved claim sheets and credit note sheets
Credit notes and ledger entries from the ERP or Tally
Distributor ledger statements in Excel, PDF or scans
outputs: Claim-to-credit-note match with missing and duplicate credits flagged
Ledger differences for each distributor, with a reason for each
Audit trail from approval to ledger entry
human_in_the_loop: Finance decides every correction. The system never raises or reverses a credit note on its own, and any difference it cannot explain is shown to a person as unexplained rather than forced into a category.
integrations: ERP such as SAP or Tally for credit notes and ledgers
Claims settlement output, from our claims system or your sheets
Distributor statements by email or upload
guardrails: No difference marked as explained without matching entries on both sides
Credit note amount always shown beside the approved amount
Corrections posted only after finance approves them
Unexplained differences stay open until a person closes them
compliance_notes: Credit notes for GST need to reference the original invoice; the system checks that each credit note carries the reference your tax team expects.
Reconciled balances with an audit trail support distributor balance confirmations at year-end audit.

rollout.scope: One quarter of approved claims and credit notes for the distributors of one region, with their ledger statements for the same period.
deliverables: Claim-to-credit-note match for the rollout period
Ledger comparison for each distributor in scope
Reconciliation statement format agreed with your team

what_we_measure.how: Count and value of credit note errors found and confirmed by finance.
Share of ledger differences the system explained, checked by finance.
Time to produce a reconciliation statement, compared with today.

faqs.q: Do we need to use your claims system for this?
faqs.a: No. It works from your approved claim sheets and credit notes as they are today. If you use our claims settlement, the link from claim to credit note is already there.

faqs.q: Our distributors send statements in different formats. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. The statements are read as they arrive, in Excel, PDF or scanned form. Anything that cannot be read with confidence is shown to a person.

faqs.q: Can it post corrections to Tally or SAP?
faqs.a: It prepares the corrections for finance to approve. Posting them to your ERP can be added once the matching has proven itself.

faqs.q: How long does it take to go live?
faqs.a: About 6 weeks from the first files to go-live. The first cycle runs beside your current process on your own data, and your team switches over once the results agree with what it would have settled.
